# Orazaka

> Orazaka is an open-source AI platform by Krizaka (Montréal): chat, documents, images, video and agents running on your own machines, with local models. A product of Krizaka (Montréal), open source under Apache-2.0. Sign-in is closed on this development site.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://www.orazaka.com/): what Orazaka is
- [Mobile app](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/mobile): recordings and screenshots of the iOS and Android app
- [Orazaka for Mac](https://www.orazaka.com/desktop): the Orazaka Desktop test build for Apple Silicon — what it does today, requirements, download
- [Packs](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/packs): the catalogue of installable offers, what each pack adds to the Studios, and how to write one
- [Models](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/models): the models Orazaka supports — what each does, where it runs, its licence and context window
- [Talk to the team](https://www.krizaka.com/contact?topic=orazaka): the contact form lives on krizaka.com

## Documentation

- [Documentation hub](https://www.orazaka.com/docs): architecture, packs and Studios, the API, administration, the CLI
- [Quickstart](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/101): Orazaka running on your machine in five minutes: install, start, ask, run a Studio.
- [Concepts](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/concepts): The whole model on one page: clients, engine, workers, packs, Studios and runs.
- [Install, update and back up](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/self-hosting): A Mac, a Linux server or from source, then health, updates, rollback and backups. Your data never leaves your machine.
- [Run a Studio](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/studio-guide): Install a Studio, run it from the web app or the terminal, read its result and its run record.
- [Content policy: you decide](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/content-policy): What Orazaka refuses by itself, what you decide, and how a run is checked before a GPU second is spent.
- [The mobile app in four steps](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/mobile): Sign in, run a Studio, ask the model, follow your jobs: four screens, each explained.
- [Packs and Studios](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/packs): The catalogue, every manifest field, and how to write, validate and install a pack.
- [API](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/api): Every REST endpoint of every service, with the authorisation rule that guards it.
- [CLI](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/cli): Every command, subcommand and option of the orazaka CLI.
- [Tools and MCP](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/tools): What a model may call during a turn: tools, MCP servers, the tool cache and the write sandbox.
- [Worker protocol](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/worker-protocol): The AMQP contract a worker speaks to join the platform, in any language.
- [Automation and the local agent](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/automation): The protocol of the local executing agent and the automation worker.
- [Jobs, schedules and automation](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/jobs): The job plane, its workers, every scheduled task and the automation connectors.
- [Models](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/models): Every supported model: where it runs, its licence and its context window.
- [Measured runs](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/measured-runs): Time, cost and parameters of the runs Orazaka made, per model and provider, failures included.
- [Administration](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/admin): What an administrator controls, and how the console is secured.
- [Architecture](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/architecture): The module map, dependencies, runtime flows, interceptor pipeline and messaging topology.
- [Authentication and sessions](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/auth): How identity, sessions and access control work, flow by flow.
- [Security policy](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/security): How to report a vulnerability and which versions get fixes.
- [Licensing](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/licensing): What Apache-2.0 covers across the repositories, and where the proprietary line falls.
- [The mobile app, screen by screen](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/mobile-guide): What the app does today, how to run it against the local stack, and which screens do not read the server yet.
- Full text of the documentation: https://www.orazaka.com/llms-full.txt

## Source

- [Orazaka repository](https://github.com/krizaka/orazaka): the engine and its workspace (Apache-2.0)

## Publisher

- [Krizaka](https://www.krizaka.com): the company that publishes Orazaka, an open-source software studio in Montréal
